To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the radionuclide activity concentrations in the granite samples were higher than those in soil samples.
the average activity concentration of radium-226 in the soil and rock samples in the study area are 14.35±0.03 and 44.99±0.03 Bq/kg, respectively.

the average value of the radionucleides Ra226, Th232 and K40 in the rock samples are higher than that in soil samples, and the total absorbed dose rate in the granite samples are higher than the permitted limits, and this can cause a health risk to local people who use granite as the interior decorative material of dwelling without radio protection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of the gamma emitting radionuclids in soil samples and granite rocks of Shabwih and Hadramout regions, Yemen.
the assessment of environmental hazards of radiation in soil and rock of Shabwaa and Hadramout regions.
the assessment and the evaluation of environmental hazards of radiation in the rock and soil samples from the Shabwah region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the natural radioactivity of the soil and rock samples of the two regions under investigation, Shabwah, and Hadramout, are within the limits recommended by the International Commission on Radiation Protection (ICRP).

the measured values of the radon gas exhalation rates, radionuclide activities, absorbed dose rates and external hazard index of the soil and rock samples in Shabwah region are less than those of Hadramout region.
the average values of the activity concentration of the natural radioactivity in the soil and rock samples from the investigated regions are not harmful.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the measured values of the radon gas emanation rate, the radium equivalent activity, the external hazard index, the absorbed dose rate, and the annual effective dose rate of all soil and rock samples of Shabw and Hadramout are less than the permissible limits.
the average values of absorbed dose rate and the external hazard index of the soil and rock samples were found to be lower than the permissible limits.
the natural radioactivity of the soil and rock samples in the study area does not pose radiological hazard to the local people.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the radionuclide concentrations in the soil samples of the two regions of Yemen are higher than those of other countries, and the concentrations in rock samples are higher than those found in other countries.
the natural radioactivity of the soil and rock samples in the study area are not harmful to human health, but the absorbed dose rate in rock samples is higher than the permissible limits.
, there is a need for further investigation of the radioactivity in the granite samples in Yemen.
